final_candidates.decision_summary: Thr-to-Ile increases hydrophobic packing near, but not within, the receptor-binding region, a frequently stabilizing conservative change. Position is outside known receptor contacts, so cell entry should be preserved.

Removing the polar hydroxyl while retaining the aromatic ring is a classic stabilizing substitution in the vestigial esterase subdomain core. It does not touch the receptor-binding site or fusion peptide.
Proline restricts unfolded-state backbone entropy, rigidifying a surface loop distant from the RBS and fusion machinery. Risk is limited to local structural tolerance of the kink.

stop_reason.detail: LLM-only control with no evidence tools; further self-review rounds are unlikely to improve the Top-3 ranking.

history.rationale: Surface-exposed HA1 residue; Glu-to-Lys can create new inter-helical/inter-protomer salt bridges without touching the receptor-binding site, mildly stabilizing the trimer.
Charge-swap could form a favorable salt bridge but risk of pH-dependent destabilization near the fusion-domain region lowers confidence. Retain for now pending further reasoning.
Region near the stem/vestibule; Thr-to-Ile replaces a polar residue with a better-packed hydrophobic side chain in a partially buried environment, a recurring theme in heat-stable HA variants.

T292 sits in a loop region of HA1 near the receptor-binding domain; substitution to isoleucine increases hydrophobic packing without changing size drastically, and Thr-to-Ile mutations frequently improve thermal tolerance. It is surface-adjacent but not a known receptor-contact residue, so cell entry should be preserved.
Loop-proline substitution can rigidify a surface loop on the HA head away from the RBS, reducing conformational entropy loss on folding while preserving entry functions.

Proline at position 138 restricts backbone entropy of the unfolded state and can rigidify a surface loop; it is distant from the RBS and fusion peptide. Ser-to-Pro is a well-known generic stabilizing substitution if the position tolerates a kink.
Conservative polar substitution on a solvent-exposed head residue; reduces charge repulsion in a Lys cluster (K136-K168) and may allow improved local packing.
Loss of positive charge may reduce repulsion in the 130-loop; effect on folding stability is speculative but plausible. Retained as a mid-tier candidate.
Tyr-to-Phe in a hydrophobic core-adjacent position of the head domain removes a buried hydroxyl while conserving packing, a classic small stabilizing substitution.

Y268F removes a polar hydroxyl while retaining the aromatic ring, commonly stabilizing buried aromatic cores; residue 268 is in the vestigial esterase subdomain and not a receptor-binding site. This is a classic stability-enhancing conservative substitution pattern.
HA2 near the fusion peptide N-terminus; Asn maintains H-bonding capacity while lowering local electrostatic strain, plausibly stabilizing the prefusion stem conformation.
Asn at 365 removes a negative charge near HA2 but is unproven; retained as a low-confidence option pending one more reasoning pass.
Solvent-exposed HA1 site; substitution of a charged Lys with Asn can relieve desolvation cost at the surface, marginally improving fold stability.
Lys118 lies near the 110-loop interacting with the fusion peptide region; charge neutralization risks affecting fusion triggering. Rejected.

Ala at 299 reduces hydrophobic packing; small-to-smaller substitutions generally destabilize cores rather than stabilize. Rejected.
